newsitem.title: USA: Aiken Cty, S.C., sues city over new tax district.
newsitem.headline: Aiken Cty, S.C., sues city over new tax district.

text.p: South Carolina's Aiken County School District has filed suit against city of North Augusta challenging the validity of a newly formed special tax district, Augusta Chronicle reported Friday.
The suit alleges the 457-acre Riverfront tax-increment financing district approved by the city council last month does not include blighted areas as required by state law.
The suit also alleges that the distict would unfairly deprive the school of any additional tax dollars stemming from property improvements in the district.
The city plans to sell $15.7 million in tax increment financing bonds to fund improvements in the area along the Savannah River.
Any new tax revennues from property improvements would go to pay debt service on the bonds. Taxes paid to Aiken County and the school district would remain frozen at the current amount for 15 years.
The area is scheduled for numerous projects, including a hotel, convention center, town center and residential development.
Mayor Thomas Greene said the district was formed legally.
"We were dealing with blighted areas and the way the tax increment financing was handled was totally proper," he said.
